_notes: SPEC §12.4 plus the v0.2 seam S2. The server draws one value from each list per boot and renders them into the boot/identity prompt as {{dice_json}} = {era_decade, setting, temperament, material_a, material_b, naming_register, strange_detail, wallpaper_motif} — the keys below are those same names. naming_register decides the SHAPE of the machine's name (BAKEOFF-2: 7 of 9 names were two nouns welded together, because nothing rolled the register). strange_detail is the session's one quietly-wrong idea, and replaces the three worked examples that used to sit in prompts/system/voice.md and came back almost verbatim on every engine. wallpaper_motif is read by the SERVER when it builds the wallpaper image prompt (seam S3, prompts/images/wallpaper.md), never by the model. Every entry is a short, common-noun string: no product names, no person names, no place names, no brand, no numeric-unit clichés. Adding entries is a data change and needs no prompt edit. Minimums: 12 era_decade, 60 setting, 30 temperament, 40 material_a, 40 material_b, 12 naming_register, 60 strange_detail, 40 wallpaper_motif. A ninth key, `reality_offset`, was added in v0.3 (H5) and is NOT one of the eight boot dice: it holds five lists of its own, is rolled once per SESSION rather than per boot, and is rendered as {{reality_json}} into the page and app turns — see its own `_shape` note.

reality_offset._shape: H5. The server (server/dice.ts `loadReality`/`rollReality`) draws one calendar_quirk, one unit_system, one place_pair and one historical_event per SESSION, rolls a scale factor of its own inside scale_factor's range, and renders the lot as {{reality_json}} into the page and app turns (prompts/user/reality.md) — which is what makes an encyclopedia page wrong in a CONSISTENT way instead of wrong at random. Rendered object: {"calendar":<quirk>,"units":{"name":<system name>,"unit_names":<its three units>},"scale":<number>,"places":<the pair, both names>,"event":<event name>}. A unit_system's three units are read by the prompts as this world's unit of distance, of mass and of duration, IN THAT ORDER, and anything else a page has to measure is named out of the same family; they are authored as trade families so the three sound like one system. Both names of a place_pair are used together, so a session's two places belong to one world. place_pair and historical_event are deliberately proper nouns — unlike the eight boot dice, whose entries are common nouns — because their job is to be the names this reality uses in place of the real ones. Every entry is short and invented; nothing here names a real place, person, product or event. Minimums: 40 calendar_quirk, 40 unit_system, 60 place_pair, 60 historical_event.
